newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No new offer expected from Boeing-EU sources.
newsitem.headline: No new offer expected from Boeing-EU sources.

text.p: Boeing Co is not expected to make any new offer to win European Union approval of its merger with McDonnell-Douglas, EU sources said on Wednesday.
Only one issue involving intellectual property rights had been solved, the sources said.
"I don't see how anything could change between now and Wednesday," one source said, referring to July 23 when the Commission is expected to make a final ruling on the deal.
"Two thirds of our main concerns have not been met. Intellectual property is the only aspect solved," the source added.
Boeing's vice president for European Affairs Jim Franks told Reuters earlier on Wednesday that Boeing had not submitted any revised offer since Tuesday afternoon.

"We have negotiated in good faith. We have taken very seriously each of the Commission's concerns and have made a sincere effort to put forward substantial remedies in each of the areas (worrying the Commission)," he said.
Sources close to the negotiations believe that the deal will effectively be blocked on Wedneswday but expect Boeing would resubmit the deal for approval at a later stage with appropriate amendments.

Anti-trust lawyers speculate that Boeing may not at this late stage in the proceedings have time to evaluate fully the financial and legal implications of any concessions it might ultimately make to salvage the $14 billion deal.
